alex: Quick sync — we're seeing ambiguity in active/active write ownership for tenants with strict residency (EU-only). Current soft-affinity is causing 0.1% of writes to be routed to non-resident region under heavy burst. Need mitigation ideas.
maria: Ugh. Is this the same window where lease-swap delay causes fallback to nearest region?
zheng: Yeah — the routing layer will fall back to nearest if primary lease not reachable. Works usually but breaks residency guardrails.
sam: Two paths: 1) stricter routing (reject non-resident writes), 2) introduce short-term write-fencing at proxy level while handoff completes. Both have tradeoffs.
alex: I want a non-invasive experiment first. Proposal: add a "X-Residency-Token" header generated at control-plane that encodes allowed regions and a lease-id. Edge proxies check header and either forward or return 409 with a structured retry hint.
maria: That avoids changing the runtime. But how do clients get the token? Do we issue per-tenant or per-session?
zheng: Per-tenant with short TTL (30s) should be enough for most bursty handoffs. Control-plane refresh on lease change.
sam: Concern: KV cache ownership. If proxy rejects, runtime might still have a hot KV cache in other region and clients will retry hot path there, causing more churn. Need a backpressure flow.
alex: Right. Plan: when proxy rejects with 409 include hint: "retry_after_regions": ["eu-west-1"], and an idempotency token. Clients retry to allowed region. We'll also add tracing tags for rejected_count.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling deploy to infra-edge (canary) scheduled for 2026-05-12T02:00Z.
maria: Small config example for header:
```
X-Residency-Token: v1;tenant=acct_123;regions=eu-west-1;lease=lease_987;exp=1712345678
```
zheng: For experiments keep default behavior unchanged (best-effort). Enable enforcement for 5% of EU tenants first. Capture metrics: rejected_writes, end-to-end latency, and failed_replicas.
sam: Also add a fallback policy on control-plane: if lease swap takes >5s, automatically extend previous lease for a short grace to avoid split-write windows. That buys time and reduces rejects.
alex: For the long-term refactor: decouple routing decisions from edge proxies. Make an independent routing-service that returns immutable routing facts (region_set, lease_id, seq). Edge reads facts and enforces. This centralizes logic and keeps proxies thin.
maria: Agree. Plus routing-service can be versioned and rolled out without touching proxies. We'll need a migration plan for cached facts TTLs.
zheng: Migration nuance: KV cache eviction must respect the seq number from routing facts to avoid stale ownership. Add seq in cache keys.
sam: Runbook note: If we start seeing >1% rejects in canary, rollback enforcement immediately and create incident-debug channel.
alex: I'll draft an RFC this week: experiment design, metrics, sample header, runbook snippets, and long-term routing-service proposal. Action items: alex write RFC, zheng prototype header check in proxy, maria prepare canary tenant list, sam write runbook fragment.
maria: ACK, will pick 200 tenants from EU pool.
zheng: I'll push a small PR with header validation and metrics.
sam: I can draft the runbook.
alex: Thanks — let's keep thread for updates. If anyone hits a blocker ping @alex and @sam. :thumbsup:
